paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When God said, "Ask, and I will give it to you!" (2 Chronicles 1:7), Solomon could have asked for anything at all. He asked for "wisdom and knowledge" so he could lead God's people (2 Chronicles 1:10). I think he knew the job was bigger than he was, and that's the best place to start.

Look at what God says back. He points to what was in Solomon's heart, and Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge instead of riches or wealth or honor for himself (2 Chronicles 1:11). God gives him the wisdom, and then adds riches and wealth and honor on top (2 Chronicles 1:12). So when you want to serve people well, ask God for what the work needs first. I have been stamping cookies a long time, and I STILL ask for help before I touch the dough.

So what does it mean for you, baker? Maybe you've got people counting on you, at work, at home or at church, and you feel the weight of it. Solomon did too, and he took it to God instead of pretending he had it handled. Don't hide the weight. Ask Him for what you need to carry it.
